positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Use Python to develop back-end applications responsible for ingesting and processing genomic data
- Work with scientists to integrate algorithms for processing genomic data into existing pipelines and optimizing them to scale
- Use Python with web frameworks such as Flask and Sanic to create internal REST APIs for managing genomic data
- Use ViewJS in conjunction with previously mentioned web frameworks to create internal tools used by scientists to manage genomic data
- Use AWS technologies such as Lambda, Step Functions, SQS, ECS, and Cloudwatch to create and maintain a processing pipeline that automatically scales based on load in order to reduce costs and deliver results to down-stream services in a timely manner
- Use monitoring tools such as Grafana, Kibana, and New Relic to monitor pipeline health
- Architect solutions to automate validation and migration processes for genomic algorithms that run on millions of customer samples

positions.title: Programmer/Analyst
positions.description:
- Create web applications used by the faculty, staff, and students of the Division of Biological Sciences.
- Use Javascript/jQuery and CSS to create front-end views to web applications that are visually pleasing, functional, and intuitive.
- Use Java on a custom web application framework running on Tomcat to create back-end business logic and data models for web applications.
- Use SQL to store data for the web applications on MySQL and Sybase servers.
- Contribute to library code (including front-end Javascript/jQuery plugins and back-end helper classes in Java)

positions.title: Technician/Helper
positions.description:
- Diagnose and repair computer software and hardware problems on computers running Windows, Mac OSX, and Linux operating systems.
- Manage cases using a case-tracking system named FogBugz.
- Respond to user requests promptly and communicate with users using phone calls and e-mails.
- Answer help desk phone calls.
- Manage distribution of IP address and office network access by activating/deactivating ports in building cores.
- Order any needed computer parts and computer software.
- Extend the support mentioned above to six buildings affiliated with the Division of Biological Sciences.
